record.original_question: What are all the 1-differential posets that do not contain [a particular induced subposet]?

evidence.quote: [Byrn2012, Conj. 6.7] What are all the 1-differential posets that do not contain [a particular induced subposet]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A locally finite graded poset $P$ with unique minimum $\hat 0$ is called a $1$-differential poset (in the sense of Stanley) if it satisfies the following two axioms:

(D1) For every pair of distinct elements $x \ne y$ in $P$, the number of elements that cover both $x$ and $y$ equals the number of elements covered by both $x$ and $y$.

(D2) For every element $x \in P$, the number of elements covering $x$ equals one plus the number of elements covered by $x$.

For a finite poset $S$, we say that $P$ contains $S$ as an induced subposet if there is an injection $\iota : S \hookrightarrow P$ such that for all $a,b \in S$ one has $a \le_S b$ if and only if $\iota(a) \le_P \iota(b)$.

Fix a particular finite poset $S_0$ (the specific obstruction subposet whose avoidance is conjectured to characterize a structurally restricted class of $1$-differential posets).

Problem. Classify, up to isomorphism, all $1$-differential posets $P$ that do not contain $S_0$ as an induced subposet. Equivalently, give an explicit list (or structural description) of every $1$-differential poset $P$ for which no induced subposet of $P$ is isomorphic to $S_0$.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of 1-differential posets remains an active open area. Byrnes (2012) classified all 1-differential lattices (only Young's lattice and the Young–Fibonacci lattice), but the broader classification questions, including those phrased as avoidance of a particular induced subposet, are not known to be resolved. There are uncountably many 1-differential posets in general, and no published classification under such an avoidance hypothesis was located.

status_evidence.title: Differential poset - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Byrnes (2012) showed that the only 1-differential lattices are Young's lattice and the Young-Fibonacci lattice. There are uncountably many 1-differential posets.
status_evidence.claim: Lattice case is settled but general classification of 1-differential posets is open.

status_evidence.title: Structural Aspects of Differential Posets (Byrnes, 2012)
status_evidence.snippet: Dissertation by P. Byrnes establishing structural results and conjectures about r-differential posets, including conjectures in Chapter 6.
status_evidence.claim: Conjectures about avoidance of induced subposets in 1-differential posets are stated in Byrnes' 2012 thesis and remain open.
